Mozilla today announced multiple new features for Firefox's AI Smart Window, which is still in the testing phase. Details are as follows.

Firefox Smart Window adds multiple new features

When Mozilla first unveiled the Smart Window a few months ago, it described the feature as "an independent, opt-in window in Firefox that lets you interact with your AI assistant of choice while you browse," and noted that it could "help you summarise content, compare tabs, organise information, or ask questions — all without breaking your flow."

Since then, the company has been gathering user feedback and today announced a series of new features designed to "help users finish what they start online."

Starting today, Firefox Smart Window will suggest groupings for related tabs — a feature particularly useful when researching a topic or planning an event and things spiral out of hand. Another especially practical new addition is automatic duplicate tab detection, allowing users to identify and close duplicate tabs with a single click.

Smart Window is also benefiting from a new partnership between Mozilla and Exa, announced today. Exa is an AI-focused search and web retrieval company, and its integration with Smart Window will "pull in fresh web information and surface sources in its answers, without sending you off to another search results page," according to Mozilla.

Lastly, Smart Window has added natural language input prompts — for example, typing "the show I was watching last week" will "show visual previews of pages from your browsing history, making it easier to spot the one you're looking for among similar results without having to open each one to check."
